TABLE: Pierro A, Pica G, Giannini AM, Higgins ET, Kruglanski AW (2018), '"Letting myself go forward past wrongs": How regulatory modes affect self-forgiveness', PLoS ONE 13(3):e0193357, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0193357 (CC BY 4.0), Study 3 (S3 File, .sav, sha256 559ce822e2bbcf07c201f02fceae41db4d4fecf5a0cb204d87a9b148124c7429), N=85 Italian students, University of Rome 'La Sapienza'. Live data: 10 items negaffect1..negaffect10, resp 1-5, n=85 per item except negaffect6 (n=84). STEP 3b PASSED -- the table really is the 10-item negative-affect half of the PANAS and not one of the other four instruments in the same S3 file (Locomotion 12 items 1-6, Assessment 12 items 1-6, self-forgiveness 4 items 1-4, positive affect 10 items 1-5). The paper's Study 3 Measures section: 'The Panas (Positive and Negative Affect Schedule) [32] was used to gauge positive (e.g., active, proud, determined) and negative (e.g., upset, guilty, distressed) emotional responses to the transgression reported... participants used a Likert-type scale... to endorse each of 20 adjectives in response to the question: "How do you feel currently about this transgression?"'. Reference [32] is Watson D, Clark LA, Tellegen A (1988) JPSP 54:1063-1107, i.e. the standard 20-item PANAS. WHY BLOCKED: the deposit publishes NO item wording and the code->adjective correspondence is not recoverable, and is not merely unverified -- the one testable ordering hypothesis is positively DISCONFIRMED. (a) The .sav carries no item wording at either label level: all 75 columns have variable label None except four ('serious subjective', 'harmful subjective', 'months since the offence occurred', the four rater columns), and the file's ONLY value-label set is gender {0 men, 1 women} -- checked both levels explicitly, per core model section 2. (b) The article's Supporting Information is exactly S1-S4 File, four .sav datasets; there is no questionnaire, codebook or item appendix, and the paper prints no item list -- only the three positive and three negative example adjectives quoted above, with no codes attached. So there is no data_labels and no paper_explicit route. (c) The only remaining route is order: assume negaffect_i is the i-th negative adjective of the canonical Watson/Clark/Tellegen sequence (distressed, upset, guilty, scared, hostile, irritable, ashamed, nervous, jittery, afraid). The data rules that out. The PANAS NA half is five near-synonym couplets, which show up in this sample as five perfectly reciprocated top-partner pairs -- {negaffect1,negaffect5} r=0.85, {negaffect3,negaffect4} r=0.73, {negaffect2,negaffect6} r=0.71, {negaffect7,negaffect8} r=0.68, {negaffect9,negaffect10} r=0.57 -- and NONE of them is a couplet the canonical ordering predicts. Canonical predicts {1,2} distressed/upset r=0.56, {3,7} guilty/ashamed r=0.35, {4,10} scared/afraid r=0.40, {5,6} hostile/irritable r=0.50, {8,9} nervous/jittery r=0.43: 0 of 5 recovered, and every one of them is weaker than the pairing actually observed. Watson & Clark's NA facets (fear/guilt/hostility/sadness) fare no better under canonical ordering: mean within-facet r = 0.449 vs mean between-facet r = 0.482, i.e. the facet structure has NEGATIVE support (-0.033). The administration evidently used a reordered adjective list, and that order is published nowhere. Assigning adjectives on canonical order would ship a confidently-wrong mapping that validate_items.R and audit_batch.R would both pass -- exactly the failure Step 5b exists to prevent. WHY NOT SHIP A BLANK-item_text TABLE: the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling ships blank item_text where the source publishes no wording; here wording exists (20 known PANAS adjectives) and is simply unattributable to codes, which is a different thing. Under the irw#1770 test -- 'does a row we ship carry the item's referent' -- the answer is no, and the referent (which adjective) is precisely what is missing, so the table would count as 'has item text' in the corpus figures while telling a reader nothing. Held, per 'err on the side of not having things'. RIGHTS, for the record, are NOT the reason for the block: instrument_rights_register.csv carries PANAS with verdict=ship, and the PANAS is SKILL.md's own worked example for the rule that a bare copyright notice on a journal article is a notice about that article, not a term over the instrument. No fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause is locatable from Watson/Clark/Tellegen. Had the mapping been recoverable, this table would have shipped. BANKED FOR A LATER PASS, so nothing has to be re-derived: (1) the administered prompt is published verbatim -- 'How do you feel currently about this transgression?'; (2) the instrument is the PANAS negative-affect subscale, 10 of the standard 20 adjectives; (3) the five synonym couplets above are already identified, so a source giving the administration order would finish this table in minutes; (4) administered language is Italian (the paper says the co-administered regulatory-mode scale was 'the same Italian version' used in Study 1, and the sample is Italian students), so had it shipped it would have been the translated_substitute fallback with language=Italian, matching the batch_137 sibling treatment of pierro_2018_assessment_s3. DATA CAVEATS, independent of the block and worth recording against the response table: (i) the paper states the PANAS was answered on 'a Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (not at all) to 7 (extremely)', but the deposit is a 1-5 scale -- every negaffect column runs 1-5 and the standard PANAS is 5-point, so the paper's '7' is an error in the paper, not a truncation in IRW; consequently the mid-scale anchors for this administration are undocumented and only the two endpoint labels are even reported. (ii) The raw .sav holds one out-of-range value 6 on negaffect6 (and one on posaffect9); data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py filters to 1-5, which is why negaffect6 has n=84 in the live table against 85 for every other item. (iii) The composite 'negaffect' column in the .sav is the plain unweighted mean of the 10 stored columns and reproduces the paper's published M=2.42, SD=.82 exactly (computed 2.4153 / 0.8176), confirming the items are stored as administered with no reverse-scoring. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE: the authors (gennaro.pica@uniroma1.it) supplying the Study 3 questionnaire or a variable codebook giving the adjective order. Nothing else reaches it -- the canonical order is ruled out by the data, so even locating a published Italian PANAS form would not settle it unless it were the form this study actually used. So this really is the PANAS Positive Affect subscale as the study scored it, and not one of the four other instruments in the same S3 file (Locomotion 12 items 1-6, Assessment 12 items 1-6, self-forgiveness 4 items 1-4, negative affect 10 items 1-5). Items are stored RAW -- no PA item is reverse-worded and none is stored recoded. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: administered in Italian (85 Sapienza students; the paper says the Italian versions of the co-administered regulatory-mode scales were used). The Italian PANAS wording is published nowhere in scope: the deposit S3 File .sav carries NO variable labels on any of its 76 columns except 'serious', 'harmful', 'time' and the four rater columns (all English, none of them items), and the only value labels in the entire file are gender {0 men, 1 women}; the article's Supporting Information is exactly S1-S4 File, four .sav datasets, no questionnaire. Base fields therefore hold the original Watson, Clark & Tellegen (1988) English, language=Italian, no _translated columns: text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. (2) MAPPING IS RECONSTRUCTED AND ONLY PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Nothing in the source ties posaffectN to an adjective; the paper reproduces only three PA adjectives, and as examples ('e.g., active, proud, determined'). item_text is assigned from the canonical PANAS printed order (PA positions 1,3,5,9,10,12,14,16,17,19 = interested, excited, strong, enthusiastic, proud, alert, inspired, determined, attentive, active). The numbering CONVENTION is corroborated on the sibling negative block of the same .sav, where canonical numbering makes two falsifiable extreme predictions for a self-committed-transgression recall and both hold: negaffect7 = 'ashamed' is the most endorsed adjective of the twenty (3.53) and negaffect5 = 'hostile' the least (1.48); the rival hypothesis that the adjectives were numbered alphabetically in Italian is refuted by the same two numbers (it would put 'ostile' at the maximum and 'vergognoso' near the bottom). What is NOT established: nothing distinguishes one POSITIVE adjective from another, and one within-block pattern sits oddly under the canonical reading -- 'alert' (posaffect6) has the highest mean at 3.53 while its near-synonym 'attentive' (posaffect9) has the lowest at 1.64. See verify_pierro_2018_posaffect_s3.R; Step 5b status PARTIAL, and public_note discloses it. (3) RESPONSE SCALE: the live data are 1-5 and the study's own composite confirms a 5-point administration, but the paper's Measures section states 'a Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (not at all) to 7 (extremely)'. The paper is wrong about the number of points -- no PA or NA column in the deposit exceeds 5 except a single stray 6 (see 4) -- while its two endpoint glosses agree with the canonical PANAS extremes. The five canonical anchors (Very slightly or not at all / A little / Moderately / Quite a bit / Extremely) are therefore shipped for all five levels rather than the paper's endpoint pair, because mixing the paper's endpoint rendering with canonical middles would produce a scale from no single source (the medvedev_2018_pan precedent). This is a deviation from the study's own printed description and is disclosed. (4) DATA DEFECT, NOTED NOT FIXED: source column posaffect9 holds one value of 6 on an otherwise 1-5 scale, and no respondent used 4 on that item. data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py filters resp to 1-5, so the stray 6 is dropped and posaffect9 has n=84 live where every other item has 85, and only levels 1,2,3,5 observed. Isolated to one item and out of range, so it is a data-entry error rather than a wider scale. Its option rows for resp=4 and resp=5 are still emitted because those levels are in the table's overall resp set. (5) TRANSCRIPTION: item_text is the bare adjective -- the instrument's real shape, no stem exists. instructions holds the paper's own rendering of the question the adjectives were rated against, 'How do you feel currently about this transgression?', quoted verbatim from the Measures section; that is English rendered by the study's authors, not the Italian participants read. section_prompt blank; single trivial section_id.
